therapies_index.name: Bariatric surgery
approved_indications: Discussed in studies of surgically induced weight loss and subsequent UI improvement; not specifically recommended as UI treatment

therapies_index.name: Smoking cessation
approved_indications: Smoking cessation strategies for patients with OAB who smoke

therapies_index.name: Anticholinergic drugs
therapies_index.mechanism: Antimuscarinic activity is described, with agents differing in muscarinic-receptor affinity and other pharmacological properties.
approved_indications: OAB after failure of conservative treatment
Urgency-predominant MUI
Nocturia in women with UUI or other LUTS
therapies_index.administration: Extended-release formulations should be considered where possible. If ineffective, the guide advises considering dose escalation, another formulation, or mirabegron alone or in combination.
key_toxicities: UTI was reported in the Panel review
monitoring: Review efficacy and adverse effects early.
Assess and monitor mental function when starting treatment in elderly patients.
Assess cumulative anticholinergic burden and associated co-morbidity.

therapies_index.name: Oxybutynin
approved_indications: Studied for OAB/UUI and nocturia associated with urinary symptoms
therapies_index.administration: Immediate-release, extended-release, transdermal and topical gel formulations are discussed. One nocturia trial used 2.5 mg immediate-release oxybutynin once daily, with possible escalation to 5 mg three times daily.
key_toxicities: Dry mouth, particularly with oral immediate-release treatment
Skin reactions leading to withdrawal with transdermal treatment
Immediate-release treatment may cause or worsen cognitive dysfunction.
monitoring: Review efficacy and adverse effects early.
Assess and monitor cognition in elderly patients receiving anticholinergics.

therapies_index.name: Fesoterodine
approved_indications: Studied for OAB/UUI
therapies_index.administration: The guide discusses 4 mg and 8 mg doses; efficacy of 8 mg, but not 4 mg, was confirmed in pooled analyses of patients aged > 75 years.
key_toxicities: Fesoterodine 8 mg daily caused more dry mouth than tolterodine 4 mg daily in cited comparisons.
monitoring: Review anticholinergic efficacy and adverse effects early.

therapies_index.name: Solifenacin
approved_indications: Studied for OAB/UUI, including the urgency component of MUI
therapies_index.administration: The guide discusses 5 mg/day and 10 mg/day.
key_toxicities: Solifenacin 10 mg daily had more dry mouth than tolterodine ER in cited comparisons.
Patients aged > 80 years experienced more frequent adverse events in a pooled analysis.
monitoring: Review anticholinergic efficacy and adverse effects early.
Assess and monitor mental function when prescribing anticholinergics to elderly patients.

therapies_index.name: Tolterodine
approved_indications: Studied for OAB/UUI, urgency-predominant MUI and nocturia associated with urinary symptoms
therapies_index.administration: Immediate-release and extended-release formulations are discussed. Nocturia studies used tolterodine 4 mg/day or tolterodine ER 4 mg.
key_toxicities: Occasional electroencephalographic changes were observed with tolterodine in healthy volunteers in cited studies.
monitoring: Review anticholinergic efficacy and adverse effects early.
Assess and monitor mental function when prescribing anticholinergics to elderly patients.

therapies_index.name: Trospium
therapies_index.mechanism: The guide notes that its hydrophilic quaternary-amine properties appear to limit passage across the blood–brain barrier in healthy people.
approved_indications: Studied for OAB/UUI
therapies_index.administration: Immediate-release formulations are included in the cited comparisons.
key_toxicities: Dry mouth is reported in comparisons of anticholinergic agents.
monitoring: Review anticholinergic efficacy and adverse effects early.

therapies_index.name: Trospium chloride
therapies_index.mechanism: The guide states that molecular properties appear to restrict entry across the blood–brain barrier in healthy individuals.
approved_indications: Studied for OAB in elderly patients

therapies_index.name: Propiverine
approved_indications: Studied for cure of UI in trials of anticholinergic treatment
therapies_index.administration: Immediate-release formulations were included in the cited trials.

therapies_index.name: Darifenacin
approved_indications: Studied for OAB/UUI, including in elderly patients
therapies_index.administration: A comparison discusses darifenacin, 15 mg daily.
key_toxicities: Dry mouth was reported in comparisons of anticholinergic agents.
monitoring: Review anticholinergic efficacy and adverse effects early.

therapies_index.name: Imidafenacin
approved_indications: Included in comparative studies of anticholinergic treatment for OAB

therapies_index.name: Mirabegron
therapies_index.mechanism: As a beta-3 agonist, stimulation of detrusor beta-3 adrenoceptors is thought to relax detrusor smooth muscle.
approved_indications: An alternative to anticholinergics for women with OAB after conservative treatment fails
Additional treatment when solifenacin 5 mg provides inadequate control
An option mentioned for urgency-predominant MUI
therapies_index.administration: Studies assessed 25, 50 and 100 mg. An RCT added mirabegron 50 mg after inadequate response to solifenacin 5 mg.
key_toxicities: Hypertension (7.3%), nasopharyngitis (3.4%) and UTI (3%) were the most common events in mirabegron groups; the overall adverse-event rate was similar to placebo.
monitoring: Offer early follow-up after starting beta-3 agonist treatment.

therapies_index.name: Vibegron
therapies_index.mechanism: Beta-3 adrenoceptor stimulation is thought to relax detrusor smooth muscle.
approved_indications: Studied for OAB/UUI; described as commercially available in some countries
therapies_index.administration: Trials assessed 75 mg or 100 mg.
monitoring: Offer early follow-up after starting beta-3 agonist treatment.

therapies_index.name: Mirabegron plus solifenacin
approved_indications: Patients whose OAB was inadequately controlled with solifenacin 5 mg
therapies_index.administration: An RCT evaluated adding mirabegron 50 mg to solifenacin 5 mg.
monitoring: Offer early follow-up after starting beta-3 agonist treatment.

therapies_index.name: Vaginal oestrogen therapy
approved_indications: LUTS with associated symptoms of GSM
Postmenopausal SUI with symptoms of vulvovaginal atrophy
Nocturia, after counselling about potential benefits and risks
therapies_index.administration: Vaginal pessaries, rings and creams are described. The optimal duration and long-term effects are uncertain.

therapies_index.name: Oestradiol
approved_indications: Vaginal treatment of postmenopausal vulvovaginal atrophy and associated urinary symptoms was studied
An oestradiol-releasing vaginal ring was studied for nocturia
therapies_index.administration: Vaginal and oral routes are discussed; the guide distinguishes local treatment from systemic HRT.

therapies_index.name: Oestriol
approved_indications: Vaginal treatment of postmenopausal vulvovaginal atrophy and associated urinary symptoms was studied
An oestriol vaginal pessary was studied for nocturia
therapies_index.administration: Vaginal pessaries and oral treatment are discussed.

therapies_index.name: Conjugated equine oestrogens
approved_indications: Discussed as systemic HRT, not as an effective SUI treatment
therapies_index.administration: Systemic and vaginal use are discussed separately.
key_toxicities: Systemic treatment increased the development or worsening of UI compared with placebo and did not improve SUI.

therapies_index.name: Tibolone
approved_indications: Named among drugs used as HRT for natural or therapeutic menopause; no UI treatment indication is given

therapies_index.name: Raloxifene
approved_indications: Named among drugs used as HRT for natural or therapeutic menopause; no UI treatment indication is given

therapies_index.name: Duloxetine
therapies_index.mechanism: Inhibits presynaptic reuptake of serotonin and noradrenaline, increasing stimulation of pudendal motor neurons and urethral striated-sphincter tone.
approved_indications: Where licensed, selected patients with SUI who have not responded to other conservative treatment and wish to avoid invasive treatment
Where licensed, selected patients with stress-predominant MUI who have not responded to other conservative treatment and wish to avoid invasive treatment
therapies_index.administration: Start and discontinue by dose titration. A cited comparison used 80 mg daily.
key_toxicities: Nausea and vomiting (> 40% of patients in two open-label studies)
Mental health problems and suicidal ideation are identified as possible adverse effects.
monitoring: Counsel carefully about adverse-event risk.

therapies_index.name: Phenylpropanolamine
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI as an adrenergic agonist; the supporting evidence was weak

therapies_index.name: Midodrine
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI as an adrenergic agonist; the supporting evidence was weak

therapies_index.name: Norepinephrine
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI in trials of adrenergic drugs

therapies_index.name: Clenbuterol
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI in trials of adrenergic drugs

therapies_index.name: Terbutaline
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI in a trial of adrenergic drugs

therapies_index.name: Eskornade
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI in a trial of adrenergic drugs

therapies_index.name: Ro 115-1240
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI in a trial of adrenergic drugs

therapies_index.name: OnabotulinumtoxinA
therapies_index.mechanism: For urethral sphincter injection, botulinum toxin inhibits presynaptic acetylcholine release and reduces sphincter tone.
approved_indications: OnabotulinumtoxinA (onabotA; BOTOX®) 100 U is licensed in Europe for OAB with persistent or refractory UUI in adults of both sexes
External urethral sphincter injection is discussed for UAB and functional BOO
therapies_index.administration: The licensed OAB treatment is bladder-wall injection of 100 U. External-sphincter injection is a separate intervention. Doses of onabotA cannot be transferred to other botulinum toxin formulations.
key_toxicities: After bladder-wall injection: UTI, increased PVR volume and voiding dysfunction that may require CISC; bacteriuria risk is high, although its clinical significance is uncertain.
After external-sphincter injection in BOO case series: UTI and temporary need for CISC.
monitoring: Before bladder-wall treatment, counsel about limited response duration, UTI and possible prolonged CISC.
Repeat bladder-wall injections as needed after an effective response, observing the manufacturer's minimum interval.

therapies_index.name: Abobotulinumtoxin A
approved_indications: Mentioned as a botulinum toxin A formulation that is not licensed for OAB/UUI

therapies_index.name: Incobotulinumtoxin A
approved_indications: Mentioned as a botulinum toxin A formulation that is not licensed for OAB/UUI

therapies_index.name: Bladder wall injections of onabotulinumtoxinA
approved_indications: OAB/UUI refractory to conservative therapy or drug treatment
therapies_index.administration: Inject onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U into the bladder wall; repeat treatment may be offered after an effective response when required.
key_toxicities: Voiding dysfunction and possible prolonged CISC
monitoring: Counsel before treatment about response duration, UTI and possible prolonged CISC.
Follow the manufacturer's guidance on the minimum interval before repeat injection.

therapies_index.name: Intra-sphincteric injection of botulinum toxin
therapies_index.mechanism: Reduces urethral sphincter tone through inhibition of presynaptic acetylcholine release; decreased urethral noradrenaline release is also proposed.
approved_indications: Functional BOO
therapies_index.administration: Injected into the external urethral sphincter; small case series in women assessed 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA.

therapies_index.name: OnabotulinumtoxinA external sphincter injections
therapies_index.mechanism: May lower outlet resistance and the guarding reflex.
approved_indications: An option before more-invasive techniques for UAB, with explicit counselling that supporting evidence is low quality
therapies_index.administration: Injection into the external urethral sphincter; symptom relief was typically three months in the cited reports.
key_toxicities: De novo SUI was reported at a low incidence.

therapies_index.name: Sacral nerve stimulation (SNS)
therapies_index.mechanism: Electrical stimulation beside sacral nerve roots modulates neural activity; the precise mechanism remains incompletely understood.
approved_indications: OAB/UUI refractory to anticholinergic treatment
UAB refractory to conservative treatment
Functional BOO, described as sacral neuromodulation
therapies_index.administration: Electrodes are placed next to sacral nerve roots and connected to a battery implanted in the buttock. Test stimulation generally precedes permanent implantation.
key_toxicities: Possible implant removal or surgical revision
monitoring: Assess response to test stimulation before permanent implantation.
Provide lifelong surveillance of an implant for lead displacement, malfunction and battery wear.

therapies_index.name: Augmentation cystoplasty
therapies_index.mechanism: A detubularised bowel segment is inserted into the opened bladder to increase functional capacity and improve compliance.
approved_indications: OAB/UUI after failure of all other treatment options, with counselling about complications
therapies_index.administration: Open and robotic approaches are described.
key_toxicities: Short-term bowel obstruction, infection, thromboembolism, bleeding and fistula
Long-term need for CISC, asymptomatic bacteriuria, bowel-symptom changes, UTI, metabolic disturbances, urinary stones, reduced renal function and bladder perforation
A small long-term risk of malignancy
monitoring: Establish willingness and ability to perform CISC before surgery.
Provide lifelong surveillance, including cystoscopic surveillance for malignancy.
Provide specialist continence or stoma-nurse support before and after surgery.

therapies_index.name: Detrusor myectomy
therapies_index.mechanism: Incises or removes detrusor muscle to create a mucosal bulge intended to increase capacity and reduce storage pressure.
approved_indications: Discussed for UUI but recommended against as its treatment
key_toxicities: Fibrosis of the pseudo-diverticulum contributed to poor long-term results in cited case series.

therapies_index.name: Urinary diversion
therapies_index.mechanism: Diverts urine from the usual bladder-outlet pathway.
approved_indications: OAB/UUI after failure of less-invasive treatment, in patients accepting a stoma and informed of the possible small malignancy risk
Intractable UI after multiple pelvic procedures, radiotherapy or irreversible sphincter damage or fistula
therapies_index.administration: Described options include ileal conduit, orthotopic neobladder and heterotopic neobladder with Mitrofanoff continent catheterisable conduit.
key_toxicities: Major short- and long-term complications are reported for urinary diversion.
monitoring: Arrange specialist continence or stoma-nurse counselling and lifelong support around major OAB surgery.

therapies_index.name: Ileal conduit urinary diversion
approved_indications: Described as an option for intractable UI requiring urinary diversion

therapies_index.name: Orthotopic neobladder
approved_indications: Described as an option for intractable UI requiring urinary diversion

therapies_index.name: Heterotopic neobladder with Mitrofanoff continent catheterisable conduit
approved_indications: Described as an option for intractable UI requiring urinary diversion

therapies_index.name: Vaginal laser therapy
approved_indications: For OAB or SUI, restricted to a well-regulated clinical research trial
therapies_index.administration: Er:YAG and Fractional CO2 lasers are discussed for SUI.
key_toxicities: Long-term safety data are lacking for OAB.
Adverse events in SUI studies were poorly and inconsistently reported.

therapies_index.name: Er:YAG laser
approved_indications: Investigated for mild SUI; vaginal laser treatment is recommended only within a well-regulated clinical research trial

therapies_index.name: Fractional CO2 laser
approved_indications: Investigated for mild SUI; vaginal laser treatment is recommended only within a well-regulated clinical research trial

therapies_index.name: Open Burch colposuspension
approved_indications: A surgical option for SUI after discussion of its risks and benefits relative to other procedures
Considered among options for complicated SUI
therapies_index.administration: Open surgical approach.
key_toxicities: Long-term POP, including enterocoele or vault or cervical prolapse and rectocele
Bladder or urethral perforation and voiding difficulties are described in comparisons.
monitoring: Arrange short-term postoperative assessment of efficacy and early complications.

therapies_index.name: Laparoscopic colposuspension
approved_indications: A surgical option for SUI after discussion of risks and benefits relative to other procedures
therapies_index.administration: Laparoscopic approach.
monitoring: Arrange short-term postoperative assessment of efficacy and early complications.

therapies_index.name: Autologous sling
approved_indications: A surgical option for SUI after discussion of risks and benefits relative to other procedures
Considered among options for complicated or recurrent SUI
therapies_index.administration: Autologous rectus sheath or fascia lata is described as the best-studied material.
monitoring: Arrange short-term postoperative assessment of efficacy and early complications.

therapies_index.name: Urethral bulking agents
therapies_index.mechanism: Intra- or peri-urethral injection forms cushions that increase resistance at the bladder outlet.
approved_indications: A surgical option for SUI after discussion of relative risks and benefits
An option for women with SUI seeking a lower-risk procedure who understand its lower efficacy, likely need for repeat injections and uncertain long-term durability and safety
therapies_index.administration: Intra- or peri-urethral injection; repeat treatment may be needed.
key_toxicities: UTI is described as the most frequent adverse event.
Peri-urethral injection may cause more urinary retention than transurethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Bulkamid®
therapies_index.mechanism: A urethral bulking product intended to increase outlet resistance.
approved_indications: Studied as an injected treatment for SUI, including primary SUI
therapies_index.administration: Urethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Macroplastique®
therapies_index.mechanism: A urethral bulking product intended to increase outlet resistance.
approved_indications: Studied as an injected treatment for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Urethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Autologous fat
therapies_index.mechanism: Investigated as an injected urethral bulking material.
approved_indications: Use as a urethral bulking agent is specifically discouraged
therapies_index.administration: Urethral injection was investigated.

therapies_index.name: Hyaluronic acid
therapies_index.mechanism: Investigated as a urethral bulking material.
approved_indications: Use as a urethral bulking agent is specifically discouraged
therapies_index.administration: Urethral injection was investigated.

therapies_index.name: Uryx™
approved_indications: Included among urethral injection products studied for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Intraurethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Contigent©
approved_indications: Included among urethral injection products studied for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Intraurethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Permacol©
approved_indications: Included among urethral injection products studied for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Intraurethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Durasphere©
approved_indications: Included among urethral injection products studied for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Intraurethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Coaptite©
approved_indications: Included among urethral injection products studied for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Intraurethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Polytef™
approved_indications: Included among urethral injection products studied for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Intraurethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Zuidex©
approved_indications: Included among urethral injection products studied for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Intraurethral injection.

therapies_index.name: Mid-urethral sling (MUS)
therapies_index.mechanism: A sling supports the mid-urethra; the guide describes reduced mid-urethral mobility after placement.
approved_indications: A surgical option for SUI after discussion of risks, benefits and alternatives
SUI surgery considered in selected women also undergoing POP repair
therapies_index.administration: Retropubic, transobturator and single-incision approaches are discussed.
monitoring: Discuss complications and alternatives before surgery.
Arrange short-term postoperative assessment; the guide supports long-term outcome assessment through registries.

therapies_index.name: Retropubic MUS
approved_indications: A route for MUS treatment of SUI, including consideration in recurrent SUI
therapies_index.administration: Retropubic insertion; the bottom-to-top and top-to-bottom directions are discussed.
key_toxicities: Higher intraoperative bladder-perforation and voiding-dysfunction risks than the transobturator route
Suprapubic pain is discussed in route comparisons.
monitoring: Counsel about route-specific risks and long-term outcomes.

therapies_index.name: Transobturator MUS
approved_indications: A route for MUS treatment of SUI
therapies_index.administration: Vagina-to-skin (inside-out) and skin-to-vagina (outside-in) approaches are discussed.
key_toxicities: Higher groin-pain risk than the retropubic route
Possible vaginal perforation, mesh exposure and repeat SUI surgery
monitoring: Counsel about route-specific risks and long-term outcomes.

therapies_index.name: Single-incision sling
approved_indications: Investigated as a surgical treatment for SUI; device-specific results should not be assumed to apply to all single-incision slings
therapies_index.administration: Single-incision insertion; Ajust® and Altis® were assessed in a comparative trial.
monitoring: Counsel that long-term efficacy remains uncertain.

therapies_index.name: Ajust®
approved_indications: Studied as a single-incision sling for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Single-incision sling placement.
key_toxicities: The guide reports mesh exposure, repeat surgery and dyspareunia for the studied single-incision sling group.
monitoring: Counsel about uncertain long-term efficacy.

therapies_index.name: Altis®
approved_indications: Studied as a single-incision sling for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Single-incision sling placement.
key_toxicities: The guide reports mesh exposure, repeat surgery and dyspareunia for the studied single-incision sling group.
monitoring: Counsel about uncertain long-term efficacy.

therapies_index.name: TVT
approved_indications: Studied as a sling procedure for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Tension-free vaginal tape placement.
key_toxicities: Suprapubic pain is discussed in comparisons of sling routes.

therapies_index.name: TOT
approved_indications: Studied as a transobturator sling procedure for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Transobturator tape placement.
key_toxicities: Groin pain is discussed for transobturator MUS.

therapies_index.name: Adjustable mid-urethral sling
approved_indications: As primary surgery for SUI, restricted to a structured research programme
Adjustable slings have been studied mainly for complicated SUI
therapies_index.administration: Sling tension can be adjusted after placement.

therapies_index.name: Remeex system
approved_indications: Investigated as an adjustable sling for SUI
therapies_index.administration: Adjustable sling placement with possible subsequent tension readjustment.
key_toxicities: Outlet obstruction prompted tension reduction in six cases in the cited study.

therapies_index.name: Artificial urinary sphincter (AUS)
therapies_index.mechanism: An implanted external-compression device provides urethral closure while allowing voiding when operated.
approved_indications: Considered for complicated SUI
Discussed for SUI caused by intrinsic sphincter insufficiency
therapies_index.administration: Implantation of an artificial sphincter.
monitoring: Before implantation, counsel about the substantial risk of complications, mechanical failure and explantation.

therapies_index.name: Adjustable compression therapy (ACT®)
therapies_index.mechanism: Adjustable balloons compress the region beside the bladder neck.
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI, particularly after failure of standard surgery or with intrinsic sphincter deficiency
therapies_index.administration: Two inflatable balloons are placed beside the bladder neck under US or fluoroscopic guidance; their volume is adjusted through subcutaneous ports.
monitoring: Counsel about complication, device-failure and explantation risks.

therapies_index.name: Vesair®
therapies_index.mechanism: The gas-filled intravesical balloon is intended to dampen bladder-pressure fluctuations during increases in abdominal pressure.
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI; the guide does not recommend routine use
therapies_index.administration: Intravesical balloon placement.
key_toxicities: Frequent withdrawal or device removal in cited trials

therapies_index.name: Mechanical devices
therapies_index.mechanism: Devices may support the bladder neck or urethra, or occlude the urethral lumen.
approved_indications: Mild-to-moderate SUI after failure of conservative treatment, only within a well-conducted research trial

therapies_index.name: Vaginal cones
therapies_index.mechanism: Used to train the PFMs.
approved_indications: Investigated for SUI; effectiveness relative to structured PFMT is inconclusive
therapies_index.administration: Intravaginal use during PFM training.

therapies_index.name: Clean intermittent self-catheterisation (CISC)
therapies_index.mechanism: Intermittently drains the bladder to address high residual volume or retention.
approved_indications: Standard treatment when patients cannot empty the bladder
Management of retention or voiding difficulty associated with BOO or after surgery
therapies_index.administration: Frequency is individualised to avoid repeated overfilling; an average of four to six catheterisations per day and 12–16 Fr catheters are described.
key_toxicities: UTI and urethral trauma are discussed as potential complications.
monitoring: Provide thorough instruction about technique, frequency, equipment and risks.
Base frequency on individual need and capability.

therapies_index.name: Indwelling transurethral catheterisation
therapies_index.mechanism: Provides continuous bladder drainage.
approved_indications: Urinary drainage only when other methods fail or are unsuitable
A possible option when a woman cannot perform CISC
therapies_index.administration: Indwelling urethral catheter.

therapies_index.name: Suprapubic cystostomy
therapies_index.mechanism: Drains the bladder through a suprapubic route.
approved_indications: Urinary drainage only when other methods fail or are unsuitable
therapies_index.administration: Suprapubic catheter placement.

therapies_index.name: Antibiotic prophylaxis
approved_indications: Patients using CISC or an indwelling catheter who have recurrent UTI, only after discussion of antimicrobial-resistance risk
key_toxicities: Increased antimicrobial resistance is a concern.

therapies_index.name: Intravesical electrical stimulation (IVES)
therapies_index.mechanism: Stimulates A-delta mechanoreceptor afferents and requires intact afferent pathways and healthy detrusor muscle.
approved_indications: Studied after prolonged bladder overdistension; routine use for UAB is not recommended
therapies_index.administration: Intravesical stimulation.

therapies_index.name: Carbachol
therapies_index.mechanism: A parasympathomimetic proposed to stimulate detrusor-cell muscarinic receptors directly.
approved_indications: Discussed as a theoretical treatment for UAB; parasympathomimetics are not routinely recommended
key_toxicities: The parasympathomimetic class is associated with gastrointestinal upset, blurred vision, bronchospasm and bradycardia.

therapies_index.name: Bethanechol
therapies_index.mechanism: A parasympathomimetic proposed to stimulate detrusor-cell muscarinic receptors directly.
approved_indications: Discussed as a theoretical treatment for UAB; parasympathomimetics are not routinely recommended
key_toxicities: The parasympathomimetic class is associated with gastrointestinal upset, blurred vision, bronchospasm and bradycardia.

therapies_index.name: Distigmine
therapies_index.mechanism: Listed as an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor among theoretical pharmacological approaches to UAB.
approved_indications: Discussed for UAB; parasympathomimetics are not routinely recommended

therapies_index.name: Pyridostigmine
therapies_index.mechanism: Listed as an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor among theoretical pharmacological approaches to UAB.
approved_indications: Discussed for UAB; parasympathomimetics are not routinely recommended

therapies_index.name: Neostigmine
therapies_index.mechanism: Listed as an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor among theoretical pharmacological approaches to UAB.
approved_indications: Discussed for UAB; parasympathomimetics are not routinely recommended

therapies_index.name: Alpha-adrenergic blockers
therapies_index.mechanism: Sympathetic blockade is intended to relax the bladder neck and urethra and lower outlet resistance.
approved_indications: An option before more-invasive treatment for women with UAB
Uroselective agents are an off-label option for functional BOO after discussion of benefits and adverse events

therapies_index.name: Tamsulosin
therapies_index.mechanism: Discussed as an alpha-adrenergic blocker intended to reduce outlet resistance.
approved_indications: Studied in women with DU, BOO or voiding symptoms

therapies_index.name: Alfuzosin
therapies_index.mechanism: Discussed as an alpha-adrenergic blocker intended to lower outlet resistance.
approved_indications: Studied in women with BOO or functional BOO
therapies_index.administration: An eight-week course was compared with placebo in a BOO subgroup.

therapies_index.name: Prazosin
therapies_index.mechanism: Discussed as an alpha-adrenergic blocker intended to lower outlet resistance.
approved_indications: Studied for voiding symptoms in women
therapies_index.administration: Compared with tamsulosin over three months in a small trial.
key_toxicities: More adverse events were reported with prazosin than tamsulosin in the cited small trial.

therapies_index.name: Intravesical prostaglandins
therapies_index.mechanism: Prokinetic activity promotes smooth-muscle contraction.
approved_indications: Postoperative urinary retention in women, only within well-regulated clinical trials
therapies_index.administration: Intravesical administration.

therapies_index.name: Prostaglandins E2 and F2
therapies_index.mechanism: Promote smooth-muscle contraction.
approved_indications: Studied intravesically for urinary retention after surgery
therapies_index.administration: Intravesical administration.

therapies_index.name: Baclofen
therapies_index.mechanism: A GABA agonist acting on sacral interneurons involved in relaxation of the striated urinary sphincter during voiding.
approved_indications: An option for women with BOO, particularly with increased EMG activity and sustained detrusor contraction during voiding
therapies_index.administration: A trial assessed oral baclofen 10 mg three times/day for four weeks.

therapies_index.name: Sildenafil
therapies_index.mechanism: Inhibits phosphodiesterase five, increasing nitric oxide levels in the female urethral sphincter to promote relaxation.
approved_indications: For women with BOO, restricted to a well-regulated clinical trial

therapies_index.name: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH)
therapies_index.mechanism: Proposed to induce urethral relaxation; its exact mechanism is unclear.
approved_indications: Discussed for BOO but specifically recommended against
therapies_index.administration: A small trial used a 200 μg intravenous bolus.

therapies_index.name: Vaginal pessary
therapies_index.mechanism: May physically reduce POP-related obstruction and improve emptying.
approved_indications: Grade three or four cystocoeles with BOO when other treatment options are unsuitable or unwanted
An option for POP management
therapies_index.administration: Intravaginal placement.
key_toxicities: Pessaries are identified as a possible rare cause of delayed vesico-vaginal fistula.

therapies_index.name: Urethral dilatation
therapies_index.mechanism: Successively larger dilators widen the urethral lumen by opening obstructing fibrotic tissue.
approved_indications: Urethral stenosis causing BOO, with advice that repeat intervention is likely
Not offered for BOO after synthetic mid-urethral tape insertion because of a theoretical mesh-extrusion risk
therapies_index.administration: Sequential dilators are used; described target calibres vary, and no standard technique is established.
key_toxicities: Theoretical urethral mesh extrusion after synthetic tape insertion
monitoring: Monitor for recurrent urethral stricture.

therapies_index.name: Internal urethrotomy
therapies_index.mechanism: Endoscopic incision opens scar tissue responsible for urethral narrowing.
approved_indications: Urethral stricture causing BOO, with postoperative self-dilatation and counselling about limited long-term improvement and UI risk
Not offered for BOO after synthetic mid-urethral tape insertion because of a theoretical mesh-extrusion risk
therapies_index.administration: Endoscopic incision; postoperative urethral self-dilatation is recommended for the stated stricture indication.
key_toxicities: Theoretical urethral mesh extrusion after synthetic tape insertion
monitoring: Monitor for stricture recurrence.

therapies_index.name: Bladder neck incision
therapies_index.mechanism: Incision of hypertrophic bladder-neck smooth muscle reduces outlet resistance.
approved_indications: BOO secondary to primary bladder neck obstruction
therapies_index.administration: Unilateral, bilateral or multiple transurethral incisions using a knife or laser are described; techniques have not been compared adequately.
monitoring: Counsel about postoperative SUI, vesico-vaginal fistula and urethral-stricture risks.
Monitor for recurrent BOO.

therapies_index.name: Urethroplasty
therapies_index.mechanism: Reconstructs a narrowed female urethra using grafts or flaps after opening the obstructing fibrotic tissue.
approved_indications: BOO due to recurrent urethral stricture after failed primary treatment
therapies_index.administration: Vaginal or labial flaps, vaginal grafts and oral mucosal grafts are described; dorsal, ventral and circumferential approaches are discussed.
key_toxicities: Possible sphincter or clitoral-body damage with a dorsal approach
Possible urethrovaginal fistula with a ventral approach
monitoring: Monitor for recurrent urethral stricture.

therapies_index.name: Urethrolysis
therapies_index.mechanism: Releases peri-urethral sutures, fibrosis or scar tissue to restore urethral mobility.
approved_indications: Voiding difficulty after anti-UI surgery
key_toxicities: De novo SUI was reported after the procedure in a cited study.
monitoring: Monitor postoperative voiding symptoms.

therapies_index.name: Sling revision
therapies_index.mechanism: Loosening, division or removal of an obstructing sling reduces outlet resistance.
approved_indications: BOO, retention or voiding problems after mid-urethral sling surgery
therapies_index.administration: Described techniques include loosening, incision or division, partial excision and removal.
monitoring: Monitor voiding, PVR volume and recurrent SUI.

therapies_index.name: Pelvic organ prolapse surgery
therapies_index.mechanism: Correcting POP may relieve urethral kinking or compression.
approved_indications: Treatment of symptomatic POP
May improve voiding symptoms when POP causes BOO
therapies_index.administration: Vaginal and abdominal approaches are discussed.
monitoring: Counsel about possible de novo SUI.

therapies_index.name: Simultaneous surgery for POP and SUI
approved_indications: Bothersome POP with symptomatic or occult SUI, only after full discussion of combined surgery versus POP surgery alone
therapies_index.administration: POP repair with a concomitant anti-incontinence procedure.
key_toxicities: More adverse events and voiding problems than POP surgery alone
Reported serious events include bladder perforation, urethral injury and tape exposure.
monitoring: Counsel about the increased adverse-event risk before combined surgery.

therapies_index.name: Desmopressin
therapies_index.mechanism: A synthetic analogue of vasopressin used to reduce nocturnal urine production.
approved_indications: Nocturia secondary to nocturnal polyuria in women, after counselling about benefits and risks
therapies_index.administration: Studies used oral bedtime doses of 0.1, 0.2 or 0.4 mg and doses of 10 μg, 25 μg, 50 μg or 100 μg; these are study regimens, not a single recommended schedule.
key_toxicities: Hyponatraemia; risk rises with age and lower baseline serum sodium.
monitoring: Monitor serum sodium carefully in elderly patients.
Avoid treatment if baseline serum sodium is below the normal range.

therapies_index.name: Desmopressin plus tolterodine
approved_indications: Investigated for women with OAB and nocturnal polyuria; the guide offers combined anticholinergic and desmopressin treatment for OAB with nocturia secondary to nocturnal polyuria
therapies_index.administration: A cited trial used once-daily desmopressin 25 μg/tolterodine 4 mg for three months.
key_toxicities: The desmopressin component carries a hyponatraemia risk.
monitoring: Monitor serum sodium carefully in elderly patients receiving desmopressin.

therapies_index.name: Furosemide
therapies_index.mechanism: Timed diuresis is intended to shift urine production to before sleep.
approved_indications: Afternoon dosing was studied for nocturia in men; no corresponding study in women is reported
The guide offers timed diuretic treatment to women with nocturia secondary to polyuria after counselling
therapies_index.administration: The cited study in men used 40 mg in the afternoon, six hours before bedtime; this is not presented as a studied dose for women.

therapies_index.name: Continuous positive airway pressure
approved_indications: Nocturia associated with obstructive sleep apnoea, following sleep-clinic assessment of suitability

therapies_index.name: Fibrin glue
approved_indications: Investigated for fistula closure in a small RCT; no significant difference from Martius flap interposition was reported
therapies_index.administration: Applied for fistula repair in the cited comparison.

therapies_index.name: Martius flap
therapies_index.mechanism: Interposes well-vascularised labial tissue to support reconstruction.
approved_indications: Discussed for selected complex or recurrent urinary fistula repairs
Discussed as an adjunct to selected urethral diverticulectomies
therapies_index.administration: Labial bulbocavernosus muscle and fat flap interposition.

therapies_index.name: Vesico-vaginal fistula repair
therapies_index.mechanism: Surgically closes the communication between bladder and vagina.
approved_indications: Persistent vesico-vaginal fistula
therapies_index.administration: Vaginal, abdominal, transvesical, laparoscopic and robotic approaches are discussed; continuous postoperative bladder drainage is recommended until healing is confirmed.
key_toxicities: Persistent or recurrent fistula or UI
monitoring: Confirm healing before ending continuous bladder drainage.
Report fistula closure and postoperative incontinence separately at a specified follow-up time.

therapies_index.name: Urethro-vaginal fistula repair
therapies_index.mechanism: Separately closes the urethral and vaginal defects, with tissue interposition when appropriate.
approved_indications: Urethro-vaginal fistula; a vaginal approach is preferred
therapies_index.administration: Reconstruction is tailored to fistula size, position, cause and tissue loss.
monitoring: Long-term follow-up may be necessary for SUI, stricture or shortening.

therapies_index.name: Ureteric stents
therapies_index.mechanism: Provide internal drainage during management or repair of ureteric injury.
approved_indications: Internal drainage or endoluminal treatment of ureteric injury or fistula
Routine prophylactic insertion during gynaecological surgery is discouraged
therapies_index.administration: Retrograde or antegrade stenting is described.

therapies_index.name: Nephrostomy
therapies_index.mechanism: Provides external upper-urinary-tract drainage.
approved_indications: Conservative or endoluminal management of ureteric injury or fistula
Diversion or palliation of selected malignant or radiation-associated fistulae
therapies_index.administration: Percutaneous nephrostomy and nephrostomy-tube diversion are described.

therapies_index.name: Urethral diverticulectomy
therapies_index.mechanism: Removes the diverticular wall and closes its urethral opening.
approved_indications: Symptomatic urethral diverticulum
therapies_index.administration: Usually transvaginal; the guide describes complete wall removal, watertight urethral closure and multilayer closure.
key_toxicities: De novo or persistent SUI or other LUTS
monitoring: Counsel about recurrence and de novo or persistent LUTS, including UI.

therapies_index.name: Marsupialisation
therapies_index.mechanism: Opens a urethral diverticulum toward the vagina to drain its contents while leaving the sac in place.
approved_indications: Described for urethral diverticulum, including decompression during pregnancy
therapies_index.administration: The diverticular wall is opened and sutured to maintain drainage.
key_toxicities: A urethro-vaginal fistula is a theoretical risk.

therapies_index.name: Endoscopic incision
therapies_index.mechanism: Widens the narrow opening of a urethral diverticulum so its sac can drain.
approved_indications: Described as a rarely reported treatment for urethral diverticulum
therapies_index.administration: Incision of the diverticular ostium using a resectoscope.

therapies_index.name: Concomitant non-synthetic sling
approved_indications: Bothersome SUI addressed at the time of urethral diverticulectomy after appropriate counselling
therapies_index.administration: Placed during diverticulectomy; contemporary reports describe pubovaginal fascial slings.
key_toxicities: Concomitant autologous pubovaginal sling placement is noted in reports of postoperative urinary retention.

therapies_index.name: Synthetic MUS
approved_indications: Not recommended as a concomitant anti-UI procedure at the time of urethral diverticulectomy
key_toxicities: Placement beside the fresh diverticulectomy suture line may increase urethral erosion, vaginal mesh extrusion, urethro-vaginal fistula and foreign-body granuloma risks.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with OAB or UUI
decision_rules: Begin with conservative measures; review comorbidities or newly introduced medicines linked to worsening symptoms.
Base fluid advice on bladder-diary measurements of intake and urine output.

recommended_regimens.name: Bladder training
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer as initial treatment for OAB/UUI.

recommended_regimens.name: Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT)
recommended_regimens.summary: Make training programmes as intensive as possible; improvement in frequency may occur.

alternative_regimens.name: Posterior tibial nerve stimulation
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider for symptomatic improvement of OAB/UUI; evidence favours it over antimuscarinics for reducing UUI episodes, without a difference for other OAB symptoms.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: An option for patients seeking symptomatic improvement.

response_assessment.method: Bladder diary
response_assessment.interpretation: Use recorded symptoms to assess change and treatment response.

supportive_care: Counsel patients about potential cognitive adverse effects when considering anticholinergic drugs.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The optimal posterior tibial nerve stimulation schedule has not been established. Evidence describes both daily and weekly schedules; a P-PTNS maintenance programme has shown benefit for up to 3 years.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with OAB who are cognitively impaired
decision_rules: Use a caregiver-initiated approach when the patient needs assistance to void.

recommended_regimens.name: Prompted voiding
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer caregiver-initiated voiding to cognitively impaired adults; short-term continence improvement is supported in care-dependent older people.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Evidence for timed voiding in cognitively impaired adults is inconsistent.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with OAB who consume caffeine, smoke, or are overweight or obese
decision_rules: Match lifestyle advice to the relevant exposure or patient characteristic.

recommended_regimens.name: Caffeine reduction
recommended_regimens.summary: Advise that reducing caffeine may improve urgency and frequency, but not incontinence.

recommended_regimens.name: Weight loss
recommended_regimens.summary: Encourage overweight or obese adults with OAB/UI to lose weight and sustain the loss.

recommended_regimens.name: Smoking cessation strategies
recommended_regimens.summary: Provide cessation strategies to patients with OAB who smoke; evidence for OAB symptom improvement is weak.

supportive_care: Review the type and amount of fluid consumed in patients with OAB (Weak).
Warn that fluid restriction may worsen constipation or cause UTI.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: In an RCT, a 25% reduction in fluid intake improved OAB symptoms but not UI; the guideline does not prescribe this reduction for every patient.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with OAB wet when active treatment is delayed, unavailable, unsuitable, unsuccessful or not desired
decision_rules: Explain available active treatments before choosing containment alone.
Use containment for temporary symptom control or when further treatment is not planned.

recommended_regimens.name: Incontinence pads and/or containment devices
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer products or devices to contain urine in OAB wet.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Containment options described include absorbent pads, urinary catheters, external collection devices and intravaginal devices.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with OAB whose conservative treatment has failed
decision_rules: Offer pharmacological treatment after unsuccessful conservative management.
Review effectiveness and adverse effects early.
If an anticholinergic is ineffective, consider increasing its dose, changing its formulation, or using mirabegron alone or with an anticholinergic.

recommended_regimens.name: Anticholinergic drugs
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer treatment for OAB; consider extended-release formulations whenever feasible (Strong).
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A Panel SR of twelve studies involving 11,179 women found significantly greater improvement in OAB symptoms than with placebo.

recommended_regimens.name: Beta-3 agonists
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer as an alternative to anticholinergics after conservative treatment fails.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Evidence summaries report that mirabegron and vibegron improve OAB/UUI symptoms more than placebo.

alternative_regimens.name: mirabegron
alternative_regimens.summary: May be used alone or with an anticholinergic when the initial anticholinergic is ineffective.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Inadequate response to an anticholinergic.

response_assessment.method: Review symptoms and adverse effects
response_assessment.interpretation: Reconsider treatment if benefit is inadequate or adverse effects occur.

supportive_care: Discuss possible cognitive adverse effects of anticholinergic treatment.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Anticholinergics produced more dry mouth, cognitive impairment, UTI and constipation than placebo in the Panel SR. Mirabegron trial adverse events included hypertension (7.3%), nasopharyngitis (3.4%) and UTI (3%); patients with uncontrolled hypertension or cardiac arrhythmia were excluded from the cited trials.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients inadequately treated with solifenacin 5 mg
decision_rules: Consider adding mirabegron rather than only increasing the solifenacin dose.

recommended_regimens.name: solifenacin plus mirabegron
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer mirabegron as add-on treatment after inadequate benefit from solifenacin 5 mg.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: An RCT found a greater likelihood of clinically meaningful UI improvement with added mirabegron 50 mg than with solifenacin dose escalation.

response_assessment.method: Review efficacy and adverse effects

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Elderly women with OAB, particularly those with existing cognitive dysfunction or risk of it
decision_rules: Use long-term anticholinergic treatment cautiously.
Assess anticholinergic burden and associated comorbidities before considering anticholinergic treatment (Weak).

alternative_regimens.name: mirabegron
alternative_regimens.summary: Pooled trials showed efficacy and safety in elderly patients.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: An alternative pharmacological option when treatment is needed; the guideline does not establish a preferred drug specifically for cognitive risk.

response_assessment.timepoint: When starting anticholinergics and during treatment
response_assessment.method: Assess and monitor mental function
response_assessment.interpretation: Consider cumulative cognitive effects; no preferred cognitive test is established.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Oxybutynin may worsen cognition in elderly women. Short-term studies have not shown cognitive dysfunction with darifenacin, fesoterodine, solifenacin or trospium; this does not establish long-term cognitive safety.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with LUTS and associated symptoms of genitourinary syndrome of menopause
decision_rules: Consider associated menopausal genitourinary symptoms when selecting local treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: Vaginal oestrogen therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer local oestrogen for LUTS accompanying genitourinary syndrome of menopause; OAB may be one component of that syndrome.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Evidence concerning women with predominantly OAB/UUI is difficult to generalise from studies focused mainly on SUI.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with OAB/UUI refractory to conservative or drug treatment
decision_rules: Offer bladder-wall injection after conservative therapy or medication has failed.
Explain the limited response duration, UTI risk and possible prolonged need for CISC before treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: onabotulinumtoxinA
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer bladder-wall injections of onabotulinumtoxinA (100 U). Repeat injections when previously effective and needed, observing the manufacturer's minimum retreatment interval (Strong).
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A pooled analysis of two RCTs reported a median of 24 weeks until retreatment was requested. Follow-up over 3.5 years found a median effect duration of 7.5 months.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Repeat as required, subject to the manufacturer's minimum retreatment interval.

not_recommended.name: Other doses of onabotA and other formulations of botulinum toxin A
not_recommended.reason: Other doses and the named alternative formulations are not licensed for OAB/UUI; doses of onabotA cannot be transferred to other brands.

response_assessment.timepoint: After injection and when considering retreatment
response_assessment.method: Assess UUI/OAB response, UTI, PVR volume and voiding difficulty
response_assessment.interpretation: An increased PVR volume may require CISC.

supportive_care: Counsel about UTI and the possible need for prolonged CISC.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Compared with placebo, onabotA was associated with significantly more voiding dysfunction and UTI at both 100 unit dose and 200 unit dose.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with OAB/UUI refractory to anticholinergic therapy
decision_rules: Offer SNS following unsuccessful anticholinergic treatment.
Use test stimulation to evaluate likely response before permanent implantation.

recommended_regimens.name: Sacral nerve stimulation
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer an implanted sacral stimulation approach for refractory OAB/UUI.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the ROSETTA trial, recurrent UTIs at two years occurred in 10% with SNS versus 24% with onabotA; SNS had a 9% removal rate and 3% revision rate at two-years follow-up.

response_assessment.method: Test stimulation
response_assessment.interpretation: The guideline identifies this as the only reliable predictor of SNS treatment success.

response_assessment.method: Implant surveillance
response_assessment.interpretation: Monitor lead displacement, malfunction and battery wear.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The ROSETTA trial found no statistically significant difference between SNS and onabotA in mean OABq-SF symptom-score improvement or reduction of mean daily UUI episodes at two years.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with OAB/UUI who have exhausted other treatment options
decision_rules: Consider augmentation cystoplasty only after all other treatments have failed and all potential complications have been explained.
Establish that the patient is willing and able to undertake CISC and understands the need for lifelong surveillance.

recommended_regimens.name: Augmentation cystoplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer only after failure of every other treatment option and comprehensive complication counselling.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a case series including 51 women with mixed idiopathic and neurogenic UUI, at an average follow-up of 74.5 months, 53% were continent and satisfied, 25% had occasional leakage and 18% continued to have disabling UUI.

not_recommended.name: Detrusor myectomy
not_recommended.reason: The guideline advises against offering it for UUI; adult case series found poor long-term results related to fibrosis.

response_assessment.method: Surveillance after augmentation cystoplasty, including cystoscopic surveillance
response_assessment.interpretation: Monitor for complications, including the small malignancy risk.

supportive_care: Arrange specialist-nurse or equivalent counselling and lifelong support before and after major OAB surgery.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Evidence specific to idiopathic OAB/UUI is limited, and short- and long-term severe complications are important risks.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with OAB/UUI who have failed less-invasive treatments, accept a stoma and have been warned about possible malignancy risk
decision_rules: Reserve diversion for failure of less-invasive therapies and obtain informed acceptance of a stoma.

recommended_regimens.name: Urinary diversion
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer only within the stated eligibility limits after discussion of complications and the possible small malignancy risk.

supportive_care: Provide specialist-nurse or equivalent counselling and lifelong support.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The described reconstructive options include ileal conduit urinary diversion, orthotopic neobladder and heterotopic neobladder with Mitrofanoff continent catheterisable conduit. Evidence is insufficient to identify which provides the greatest QoL improvement.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients considering vaginal laser treatment for OAB symptoms
decision_rules: Restrict vaginal laser treatment to an appropriately regulated research trial.

not_recommended.name: Vaginal laser therapy outside a well-regulated clinical research trial
not_recommended.reason: Short-term symptom improvement is minimal, study quality is weak, and long-term effectiveness and safety data are lacking (Strong).

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with SUI, including elderly, pregnant and postpartum women; also women with MUI
decision_rules: Start with supervised intensive training before considering invasive surgery.
Balance the benefits and low adverse-event rate of PFMT against the expected effects and complications of SUI surgery.

recommended_regimens.name: Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT)
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer supervised, maximally intensive PFMT as initial therapy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A Cochrane review found that women with SUI receiving PFMT were eight times more likely to report cure than women receiving no treatment or inactive control.

alternative_regimens.name: Electrical stimulation
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider for SUI treatment or to assist teaching a PFM contraction.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: An optional treatment or teaching adjunct (Weak).

response_assessment.timepoint: After sufficient time to demonstrate a therapeutic effect
response_assessment.method: Assess SUI symptoms and response to PFMT

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Adding biofeedback to adequately matched PFMT has not shown extra benefit. Evidence about adding electrical stimulation to PFMT conflicts.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Overweight or obese women with LUTS/SUI
decision_rules: Encourage sustained weight reduction as part of conservative care.

recommended_regimens.name: Weight loss
recommended_regimens.summary: Encourage weight reduction and maintenance of the loss; evidence supports improvement in UI with non-surgical weight loss.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Surgical weight loss has also been associated with improved UI in obese women, but the guideline does not prescribe bariatric surgery specifically as SUI treatment.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Postmenopausal women with SUI and symptoms of vulvovaginal atrophy
decision_rules: Offer local oestrogen when SUI coexists with symptomatic vulvovaginal atrophy.

recommended_regimens.name: Vaginal oestrogen therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer vaginal treatment in this postmenopausal population; short-term SUI symptom improvement has been reported.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The ideal treatment duration and long-term effects are uncertain. In women taking oral conjugated equine oestrogen as HRT who develop or experience worsening SUI, discuss alternative HRT (Strong).

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Selected patients with SUI unresponsive to other conservative treatments who wish to avoid invasive treatment, where duloxetine is licensed
decision_rules: Discuss the likelihood of benefit and adverse effects carefully before prescribing.
Titrate the dose when starting and withdrawing treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: Duloxetine
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer only to selected eligible patients; improvement is possible but cure is uncommon.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: One cited study reported UI cure in 10% of patients. Two open-label studies reported nausea and vomiting in > 40% of patients.

response_assessment.method: Review benefit and adverse effects
response_assessment.interpretation: Adverse effects can lead to treatment discontinuation.

supportive_care: Counsel about gastrointestinal and central nervous system adverse effects, including reported mental health problems and suicidal ideation.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Dose titration during initiation and withdrawal is a Strong recommendation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with SUI considering surgery after exploring or failing conservative treatment
decision_rules: Offer a choice of appropriate operations and compare their benefits and harms through shared decision-making.
Follow applicable national or local restrictions on mesh surgery.
Use new SUI devices only in a structured research programme, with outcomes captured in a registry or well-regulated trial.

recommended_regimens.name: Colposuspension
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer open or laparoscopic surgery following detailed comparison with other surgical approaches.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A Cochrane review reported complete continence rates of 85–90% within the first year after open colposuspension and estimated that around 70% of women could be dry at five years.

recommended_regimens.name: Autologous sling
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer after discussing relative benefits and risks of alternative operations.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a cited RCT, continence at five years was 30.8% with fascial slings versus 24.1% with Burch colposuspension.

recommended_regimens.name: Mid-urethral sling (MUS)
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer after discussing complications, mesh concerns and all alternative treatments.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A Cochrane meta-analysis reported short-term subjective cure rates of 71–97% for retropubic and 62–98% for transobturator slings; the guideline reports superior longer-term outcomes with the retropubic route.

recommended_regimens.name: Urethral bulking agents
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer following a comparison with other operations, including their greater likelihood of SUI cure.

not_recommended.name: Vaginal laser therapy outside a well-regulated clinical research trial
not_recommended.reason: Do not offer for SUI outside research because the available evidence has important methodological and long-term follow-up limitations (Strong).

response_assessment.method: Assess treatment efficacy and early postoperative complications

supportive_care: Explain limitations of long-term mesh safety evidence and the potential complications of synthetic MUS.
Arrange appropriate long-term follow-up and support recording surgical outcomes and complications.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The named surgical options are choices requiring individual discussion, not a ranking that applies to every woman.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women requesting a lower-risk SUI procedure and accepting lower efficacy, probable reinjection and uncertain long-term durability and safety
decision_rules: Offer bulking only after explaining its efficacy and safety relative to other surgical procedures.

recommended_regimens.name: Urethral bulking agents
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer as a lower-risk procedural choice with an explicit discussion of likely repeat injections.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a cited trial of primary SUI, objective cure by negative cough stress test occurred in 66.4% with Bulkamid® versus 95.0% with TVT.

not_recommended.name: Autologous fat and hyaluronic acid as urethral bulking agents
not_recommended.reason: Do not offer because of greater adverse-event risk, including reported fatal embolism with autologous fat and local abscess with hyaluronic acid (Strong).

response_assessment.method: Assess continence, need for reinjection and adverse events
response_assessment.interpretation: Sustained benefit may require additional injections.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline finds no evidence that one bulking-agent type is superior to another.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women considering a retropubic, transobturator or single-incision MUS
decision_rules: Explain the better long-term outcomes reported with retropubic rather than transobturator insertion.
When offering a single-incision sling, distinguish apparently equivalent short-term efficacy for Ajust® and Altis® from uncertain long-term efficacy.

recommended_regimens.name: Mid-urethral sling (MUS)
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer an MUS after informed comparison with other SUI procedures and discussion of route-specific and mesh complications.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a cited equivalence trial, objective cure at 24 months was 77.3% for retropubic and 72.3% for transobturator surgery; equivalence could not be confirmed at 24 and 60 months.

alternative_regimens.name: Ajust® and Altis® single-incision slings
alternative_regimens.summary: A cited trial found non-inferior patient-reported success against conventional MUS at fifteen months, with similar reported success at 36 months; longer-term efficacy remains uncertain.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When a single-incision device is offered after counselling about its distinct evidence and adverse-event profile.

response_assessment.method: Assess continence and complications
response_assessment.interpretation: Retropubic and transobturator results may diverge over longer follow-up.

supportive_care: Discuss risks of bladder perforation, voiding dysfunction, groin pain, mesh exposure and possible further surgery as applicable to the approach.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Retropubic insertion has greater bladder-perforation and voiding-dysfunction risks; transobturator insertion has greater groin-pain risk.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with recurrent or complicated SUI, including those with prior anti-incontinence surgery
decision_rules: Provide care in centres with appropriate experience.
Evaluate the cause of recurrent leakage and individual factors carefully; consider cystoscopy and multichannel urodynamics where appropriate.
Explain that a procedure used as second-line treatment generally has lower efficacy and greater complication risk than when used first-line.

alternative_regimens.name: Secondary synthetic sling
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider as an option, while recognising that comparative findings for recurrent SUI are inconsistent.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Following individual evaluation (Weak).

alternative_regimens.name: Bulking agents
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider among the surgical options for complicated SUI.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Following individual evaluation (Weak).

alternative_regimens.name: Burch colposuspension
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider as a possible repeat operation; evidence does not establish a best procedure for recurrent SUI.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Following individual evaluation (Weak).

alternative_regimens.name: Autologous sling
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider for recurrent SUI; limited evidence suggests better results than repeat Burch colposuspension.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Following individual evaluation (Weak).

alternative_regimens.name: Artificial urinary sphincter (AUS)
alternative_regimens.summary: Consider for complicated SUI, with counselling about complications, mechanical failure and explantation.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Selected women after individual evaluation (Weak).

response_assessment.method: Clinical evaluation, with further investigation as appropriate
response_assessment.interpretation: Distinguish persistent or recurrent SUI from de novo UUI or their combination.

supportive_care: Discuss realistic second-line outcomes and procedure-specific complications.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Available evidence does not support a firm choice of best operation for recurrent SUI.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women considering an adjustable mid-urethral sling as their primary SUI operation
decision_rules: Restrict primary use of an adjustable sling to a structured research programme.

not_recommended.name: Adjustable mid-urethral sling as primary surgery outside a structured research programme
not_recommended.reason: Primary use is restricted to research because comparative evidence is insufficient and superiority over standard MUS has not been established (Strong).

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Adjustable slings are more commonly used for complicated SUI; devices have differing designs.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women receiving AUS or ACT® for SUI
decision_rules: Explain that cure is possible but that complications, mechanical failure and device removal remain substantial risks even in expert centres.

alternative_regimens.name: Artificial urinary sphincter (AUS)
alternative_regimens.summary: A compression-device option for selected complicated SUI, particularly sphincter insufficiency.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Individualised selection after counselling (Weak as an option for complicated SUI).

alternative_regimens.name: ACT®
alternative_regimens.summary: An adjustable compression-device option that may improve SUI.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Selected women after explanation of device-related risks.

response_assessment.method: Assess continence, mechanical function and complications
response_assessment.interpretation: Revision or explantation may be necessary.

supportive_care: Counsel explicitly about possible explantation and mechanical failure (Strong).
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The evidence largely concerns recurrent or complicated SUI; these devices have also been considered in uncomplicated SUI.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with mild-to-moderate SUI after failed conservative treatment who are considering a mechanical device
decision_rules: Limit mechanical-device treatment to a well-conducted research trial.

not_recommended.name: Mechanical devices outside a well-conducted research trial
not_recommended.reason: Controlled-trial evidence is insufficient to establish benefit over no treatment or a preferred device (Strong).

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Obese women considering SUI surgery
decision_rules: Explain the increased surgical risks and lower probability of benefit.
supportive_care: Provide preoperative risk-and-benefit counselling (Weak).
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Surgery may be performed safely, but outcomes may be inferior.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Older women considering SUI surgery
decision_rules: Explain potentially higher surgical risks and a lower probability of benefit.
supportive_care: Provide individualised preoperative counselling (Weak).
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Evidence about the effect of age on surgical outcomes conflicts; no operation has established superior efficacy or safety specifically in older women.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with MUI, including elderly and postpartum women
decision_rules: Treat the symptom the patient finds most troublesome first (Weak).
Begin with conservative treatment directed at the most bothersome symptom and reserve surgery as a last resort.

recommended_regimens.name: Bladder training
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer as initial treatment for MUI.

recommended_regimens.name: Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT)
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer supervised intensive training as initial treatment.

response_assessment.method: Assess the stress and urgency components separately
response_assessment.interpretation: Use the remaining most bothersome symptom to guide further treatment.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: PFMT appears less effective for MUI than for SUI alone. Combining bladder training with PFMT may be beneficial.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with urgency-predominant MUI
decision_rules: Direct pharmacological treatment towards the urgency component when it predominates.

recommended_regimens.name: Anticholinergic drugs
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer for urgency-predominant MUI; limited evidence supports improvement of the UUI component.

recommended_regimens.name: Beta-3 agonists
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer as a pharmacological option for urgency-predominant MUI.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited MUI trial of tolterodine ER found improvement in UUI but not SUI.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Selected patients with stress-predominant MUI who have not responded to other conservative treatments and want to avoid invasive therapy, where duloxetine is licensed
decision_rules: Discuss adverse-event risk carefully before offering treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: Duloxetine
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer to selected eligible patients; cited studies report improvement in incontinence but frequent adverse events.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In one MUI RCT, the duloxetine group had a treatment-emergent adverse-event rate of 61.3% and discontinuation rate of 15.7%.

response_assessment.method: Review efficacy and adverse effects

supportive_care: Counsel about the risk of adverse events.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited trial reported higher adverse-event rates in participants also taking antidepressant agents.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with MUI considering surgery for its stress component
decision_rules: Prioritise the most bothersome symptom (Weak).
Explain that SUI surgery is less likely to cure UI in MUI than in SUI alone and that other components may still require treatment.

alternative_regimens.name: Anti-incontinence procedures described for stress urinary incontinence
alternative_regimens.summary: Surgical options for the stress component are those described for SUI; the evidence does not establish which operation is preferable for MUI.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Individualised consideration after counselling about the reduced likelihood of overall cure.

response_assessment.method: Assess stress leakage and pre-existing urgency symptoms
response_assessment.interpretation: The response of urgency symptoms is unpredictable.

supportive_care: Warn about the lower likelihood of surgical success than with SUI alone (Strong).
Explain that a single treatment may not address every incontinence component (Weak).
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Evidence is inadequate to guide a particular operation for women with MUI.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with UAB and incomplete bladder emptying
decision_rules: Use measures that improve emptying while considering the risk of bladder overdistension.
Offer alpha-adrenergic blockers before more-invasive techniques (Weak).

recommended_regimens.name: Double voiding
recommended_regimens.summary: Encourage in women unable to empty the bladder completely.

recommended_regimens.name: Alpha-adrenergic blockers
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer before invasive treatment; these medicines may increase voided volume and reduce PVR volume.

not_recommended.name: Parasympathomimetics as routine treatment
not_recommended.reason: Do not routinely recommend them because clinical or urodynamic improvement is not supported and frequent or serious adverse effects may occur (Strong).

not_recommended.name: Intravesical electrical stimulation as routine treatment
not_recommended.reason: Do not routinely recommend it in women with UAB; lasting efficacy has not been established (Weak).

response_assessment.method: Assess bladder emptying, complications and the response to treatment
response_assessment.interpretation: Visit intervals depend on patient characteristics, treatment and urinary-complication frequency.

supportive_care: Warn women using abdominal straining to empty about POP risk (Weak).
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The described assisted-voiding manoeuvres have not shown efficacy in an RCT.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients unable to empty the bladder adequately
decision_rules: Use CISC as the standard approach to bladder drainage.
Choose catheterisation frequency according to individual needs and capability to avoid repeated overfilling.

recommended_regimens.name: Clean intermittent self-catheterisation (CISC)
recommended_regimens.summary: Use for patients unable to empty their bladder, with thorough instruction on technique and risks (Strong).
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: The average frequency described is four to six times per day, adjusted to individual need.

alternative_regimens.name: Indwelling transurethral catheterisation or suprapubic cystostomy
alternative_regimens.summary: Offer only if other drainage methods have failed or are unsuitable.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: When other urinary drainage options cannot be used (Weak).

response_assessment.method: Assess emptying and urinary complications

supportive_care: Provide detailed instruction on CISC equipment, frequency, technique and adverse effects.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The document does not establish that one intermittent-catheter type or regimen is superior.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with UAB refractory to conservative treatment
decision_rules: Offer sacral nerve stimulation after conservative treatment fails.
Consider external-sphincter onabotulinumtoxinA injections before more-invasive techniques only after explaining the low quality of supporting evidence.

recommended_regimens.name: Sacral nerve stimulation
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer to women with refractory UAB.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A cited meta-analysis of seven studies found a mean PVR volume reduction of 236 mL and mean voided-volume increase of 299 mL.

alternative_regimens.name: onabotulinumtoxinA external sphincter injections
alternative_regimens.summary: May improve voiding by reducing outlet resistance, but supporting evidence is limited.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Before more-invasive techniques, after explaining evidence limitations (Weak).

not_recommended.name: Detrusor myoplasty as routine treatment
not_recommended.reason: Do not routinely offer for DU because evidence of effectiveness is very limited (Weak).

response_assessment.method: Assess spontaneous voiding and PVR volume
response_assessment.interpretation: Selection for SNS is important because response varies.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The reported duration of symptom relief after external-sphincter onabotulinumtoxinA injections is typically three months.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with urinary retention after surgery
decision_rules: Restrict intravesical prostaglandins to a well-regulated clinical trial.

not_recommended.name: Intravesical prostaglandins outside a well-regulated clinical trial
not_recommended.reason: Only trial-based use is advised because evidence for successful postoperative voiding has very low certainty (Weak).

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Women with functional BOO
decision_rules: Target relaxation of the pelvic floor during voiding.
Discuss possible benefits and harms before offering an off-label uroselective alpha-blocker.

recommended_regimens.name: Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT)
